_why:
Five edges around the U.S. Navy, plus one Sol Foundation affiliation. Every source opened and read.

A process note that matters. The automated read of Ryan Graves's written testimony returned his squadron as 'commanding officer of the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program', which is not Graves and not in the document. Pulling the PDF and extracting the text directly gives what he actually wrote: 'My name is Ryan "FOBS" Graves and I am a former F-18 pilot with over a decade of service in the U.S. Navy, including two deployments in Operation Enduring Freedom and Operation Inherent Resolve.' A summariser inventing a plausible military title is exactly the failure this board exists to guard against, and it would have shipped as a sourced Tier 1 claim if the PDF had not been opened.

us-navy -> roosevelt-2014-2015 is tier 2 rather than tier 1 on purpose. The DoD release of 27 April 2020 dates two of the three videos to January 2015, and Graves's testimony places his squadron's encounters in the W-72 warning area off the east coast from 2014. Neither document names the USS Theodore Roosevelt. The carrier association is well attested elsewhere but is not in the two primary documents cited here, so the edge says so rather than borrowing the certainty.

marik-von-rennenkampff -> sol-foundation is also tier 2 and its note is rewritten. It had quoted a Sol Foundation author note - 'He delivers the Sol Briefing, the Sol Foundation's monthly update on UAP news, and has been a regular contributor to The Hill.' What the foundation's own site carries is that he is a Sol Foundation Fellow and the author of 'The Civilizational Risks of a UAP Technology Arms Race: Nonhuman Technology and Global Security'. The briefing-series role was not found there and is not asserted.

sources.name: Statement by the Department of Defense on the Release of Historical Navy Videos, 27 April 2020

edges.note: The Department authorised release of three unclassified Navy videos, one from November 2004 and two from January 2015, stating that 'the U.S. Navy previously acknowledged that these videos circulating in the public domain were indeed Navy videos' and releasing them 'in order to clear up any misconceptions by the public on whether or not the footage that has been circulating was real'. The Department's own characterisation of what they show has not moved: 'The aerial phenomena observed in the videos remain characterized as unidentified.'

sources.name: Statement by the Department of Defense on the Release of Historical Navy Videos, 27 April 2020
Ryan Graves, written testimony to the House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs, 26 July 2023

edges.note: Two of the three videos the Department released in April 2020 are dated January 2015, and Graves's testimony places his squadron's encounters in the W-72 warning area off the east coast, beginning more than a decade before he testified: 'my squadron began witnessing advanced UAP demonstrating complex maneuvers on a regular basis'. Tier 2 because neither primary document names the USS Theodore Roosevelt. The carrier association is well attested elsewhere; it is not in the two documents cited here.

sources.name: U.S. Navy press release, 'Establishment of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force', 14 August 2020

edges.note: 'Deputy Secretary of Defense David L. Norquist approved the establishment of an Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP) Task Force (UAPTF)' on 4 August 2020, with the Department of the Navy leading it under the cognizance of the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security. Its stated mission was 'to detect, analyze and catalog UAPs that could potentially pose a threat to U.S. national security'. The task force was disestablished two years later on the Deputy Secretary's direction when AARO stood up.

sources.name: Ryan Graves, written testimony to the House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs, 26 July 2023

edges.note: In his own words: 'My name is Ryan "FOBS" Graves and I am a former F-18 pilot with over a decade of service in the U.S. Navy, including two deployments in Operation Enduring Freedom and Operation Inherent Resolve.' He joined the Navy in 2009, describes the encounters in the W-72 warning area, and states 'I founded Americans for Safe Aerospace to create a center of support, research, and public education for aircrew impacted by UAP encounters', reporting nearly 5,000 members and more than 30 witnesses working with the organisation.

The Sol Foundation identifies von Rennenkampff as a Sol Foundation Fellow and carries his paper 'The Civilizational Risks of a UAP Technology Arms Race: Nonhuman Technology and Global Security', which argues for international cooperation on UAP technology development. Garry Nolan is listed as Executive Director of the Board. Tier 2: the foundation's public pages read here do not carry the Science and Policy Briefings series, so his role in it is not asserted from this source.
